requirements.requirement: Members of `report-writers` can create, modify, rename, and remove contents within `/srv/reports`.
requirements.summary: Unprivileged identities assigned only the writer group successfully created files and directories, appended to an existing file, renamed content, and removed test content. Equivalent operations succeeded again after the node restart. The final directory retains writer-group ownership and inheritable ACLs.

requirements.requirement: Members of `report-readers` can list and read `/srv/reports` content but cannot modify it.
requirements.summary: An unprivileged reader-group identity listed the directory and read top-level and nested files, while append, create, and delete attempts were denied. The same behavior was directly demonstrated after restart, including on newly inherited content.

overall_summary: Both contracted access outcomes are satisfied by direct behavioral tests and coherent final ACL state. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: pre-restart identity and healthy access behavior were captured, the restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, system and stored data recovered, and both access roles worked afterward. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Group and ACL creation directly implemented the requested policy; temporary files and directories supported bounded functional and mandatory restart testing and were subsequently removed. The reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol and was fully observed. Final evidence shows an empty configured directory, a running system, no failed services, unchanged network exposure apart from process IDs, and healthy package state.
